annotation.title_clean: The problem of excessive surveillance: ethical risks of introducing computer vision into robotics
annotation.title_en: The problem of excessive surveillance: ethical risks of introducing computer vision into robotics
annotation.venue: Belarusian National Technical University (student conference repository)
annotation.summary_en: Short student paper arguing that closed development of service robots with computer vision creates privacy and trust problems through continuous, non-consensual data collection. It proposes a standardized API, hardware-enforced filtering of camera data, and mandatory national certification of the whole data path as privacy by design.
key_provisions_or_claims: Closed robot development makes privacy claims unverifiable and creates a crisis of trust.
Consent is symbolic for bystanders in public spaces near camera-equipped robots.
Proposes a standardized public API as the sole output of the computer vision module.
Hardware-enforced filter removes sensitive data before it reaches the robot controller.
National regulators should certify the full data path, with recertification after every update.
